title: RateCap Signalboard: per-key & per-route analytics + quick-mitigation (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a working sketch and prioritized backlog for a new Console panel concept — the "RateCap Signalboard" — that unifies per-key and per-route rate/quota telemetry with quick mitigation controls and a small-slice simulator for SLA impact. Aim: reduce time-to-triage for incidents, make throttle/quotas decisions visible to product and SRE, and enable on-the-fly mitigation without having to open multiple pages.

Background / pain we're solving:
- On-call and CS currently jump between the per-credential usage page, quota config, and logs to diagnose throttles.
- Customers ask for a single-pane view showing: token/req velocity by key, dominant routes driving usage, active throttles (and why), and fast rollback/fallback toggles.
- We also need a way to simulate the impact of temporary quota bumps on SLA/cost before making changes.

High-level goals:
1) Single view for triage: timeline + table + route breakdown + key profile card.
2) One-click mitigations: temp-bump quota, enable-burst, route-allow-listing, fallback routing to cheaper model tier.
3) Clear causality: show which routes (and payload size distributions) are responsible for token spikes.
4) Auditability: snapshot export that includes pre/post config, reasoning, and a link to the ticket.
5) Lightweight simulator: estimate cost delta and latency change when switching routing policy or bumping quota.

Signalboard sketch (layout notes):
- Top: global filter bar (time range quick picks, tenant/credential picker, route regex filter, tag slices).
- Left column (30%): credential summary card for selected key (owner, tier, quota window, current usage %, active throttles). Show small sparkline for tokens/sec and P50/P95 latency.
- Center column (50%): timeline heatmap spanning selected range. Rows = routes (top N by token volume) + aggregated other. Hover on a cell shows sampled request examples (path, size, user-agent). Timeline supports scrubber + anomaly badges flagged by model (see detection rules below).
- Right column (20%): quick actions + recent changes. Actions: temporary quota bump (dropdown: +10%, +25%, custom), enable-burst toggle (30s/2m/5m), fallback route selector (map to model variants), mute alerts for key (with TTL). Below actions: recent config changes with small diff, and a button to create incident snapshot.

Per-route breakdown panel (modal or inline expansion):
- When expanding a route row: show token distribution by request size buckets, typical prompt templates (top 5), associated embedding vs. generation calls, and percent of total cost. Include a small "why this route matters" text derived from heuristics (e.g., high token size + high QPS).

Interactions and microcopy notes:
- Default time window is 1h sliding window; quick choices 5m/15m/1h/24h. For incident triage, show both sliding (last hour) and daily for trend context.
- Quota bump flow must be explicit: select duration (max 24h by default), auto-revert checkbox, optional reason field required for audit. Show estimated cost delta before confirm.
- Toasts: changes show ephemeral toast with link to snapshot and rollback. On error show clear diagnosis (e.g., "quota bump failed: limit locked by policy X").
- Anomaly badges: colors follow alert severity tokens used in Console (info/warn/error). Hover reveals contributing features (sudden QPS increase, skewed route, payload size growth).

Detection rules (proto):
- Rule A: token rate increases >3x baseline over 5 min and sustained for 2 consecutive 1-min buckets -> badge Severity: warn.
- Rule B: route contribution >40% of tokens and increase >50% vs baseline -> badge Severity: high.
- Rule C: latency P95 degradation coupled with throttle events -> badge Severity: critical.
(These will be refined in infra/observability spec INF-2345)

Simulator: what it does and UI notes
- User picks: action (quota bump, enable-burst, route-fallback), duration, traffic slice (all, user cohort, route regex).
- Output: estimated token count delta, estimated added cost (USD/day), expected change to P95 latency (qualitative: improve/neutral/worse), and risk score (0–100).
- Keep simulator optimistic: show a range (best/worst) and call out uncertainty if sampling is sparse.

Query/Export: incident snapshot
- Snapshot includes: filters, timeline screenshot, top contributing requests (sampled), config before/after, cost simulator results, and free-text field for incident notes. Export as JSON or PDF. Attach snapshot to Jira ticket via one-click.

Accessibility & performance constraints
- Timeline should progressively load top routes and lazy-load the rest.
- Provide keyboard shortcuts: focus search (f), expand top route (enter), open quick-action (k).
- Ensure heatmap cells are accessible textually for screen readers with summary tooltip text.

Backlog (near-term, prioritized):
- P0: basic panel with credential card + timeline + action panel (INF-2345).
- P0: implement temp-quota bump API endpoint contract with backend (backend ticket: BE-678).
- P1: per-route inline expansion with token buckets and sampled requests.
- P1: simulator MVP with cost model integration (link to optimize service).
- P2: anomaly detector tuning and user controls for thresholds.
- P2: incident snapshot export and Jira integration UX.
- P3: cohort comparison (compare two keys side-by-side), percent-change sparklines.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should quick actions be limited by RBAC? (Yes — admin vs read-only). Need mapping for roles and temporary grant flows.
- Auto-revert default duration: 1h vs 24h? Ops prefers 1h; CS often asks 24h. Suggest default 1h, but make policy configurable per org.
- Simulator complexity: how much historical smoothing do we apply vs real-time? Ops wants immediate numbers; product wants conservative ranges.

Next steps / ownership:
- Priya: consolidate infra contracts required (BE-678, INF-2345) and drive proto with SRE.
- Elena: quick visual mockups for three screen widths (desktop, tablet, narrow) — due Jan 29 (loom walkthrough).
- Samir: spike on sample extraction API for sampled requests in timeline hover (due Feb 5).

Related links and references:
- Console existing per-key page: confluence.redwood/console/per-key-usage (reference)
- Ticket for quota automation: JIRA: QTA-1120
- Slack discussion: #product-console pinned messages (Jan 22 thread)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a working sketch. Focus feedback on required data points for triage and the minimal set of quick actions we should expose. If we try to solve too many mitigation flows in one panel we lose clarity; prefer a focused MVP (timeline + credential card + temp-bump + fallback).
- Mark comments inline in this doc or leave reactions on the Loom mockup.

----
Quick grooming outcomes from Jan 26 sync (raw bullets):
- Keep default view to show top 10 routes; allow show-all toggle.
- Action surface should be compact — primary action = "temporary quota bump". Secondary actions behind ellipsis.
- Audit trail must include who clicked action and reason; attach snapshot to ticket automatically when source is from SRE.
- Add a small "cost impact" chip next to quota numbers for quick visibility.

End.
